long_biography.plain_text:
Sonoma began with a neglected wood-fired oven in Bellata, rural New South Wales. Andrew Connole, his father Kerry and brother Christian restored the bakery without prior baking experience. Connole then travelled to Northern California, learning from oven builder Alan Scott and sourdough baker Chad Robertson. He returned with a starter and a conviction that slow fermentation could support an Australian artisan bakery.

For two years, the family made weekly thousand-kilometre round trips between Terrigal, Bellata and Sydney, baking through the night and selling at Paddington Markets. Demand eventually moved production to Sydney, where Sonoma developed a wholesale and neighbourhood retail business. Connole has kept that founder-led platform active: the company later acquired the Berkelo bakery brand, extending the same bread-making focus across additional Sydney communities.
